title: Arakhin 30
description: Why Rav Anan could not settle his doubt from Shmuel, the mouse and the hole, a field bought before Rosh HaShana full of produce, a field sold on to a second buyer or changed in value, the Hebrew slave who is redeemed with the upper hand, Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina on the gradual decline of one who trades in Sabbatical-Year produce, and why one may not borrow to redeem a sold field but may to redeem a consecrated one.

a1.he: וְרַב עָנָן בָּרָיְיתָא לָא שְׁמִיעָא לֵיהּ, וְדִשְׁמוּאֵל מִמַּאי דְּאֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה וּמָעוֹת חוֹזְרִין? דִּלְמָא אֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה וּמָעוֹת מַתָּנָה, מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמְּקַדֵּשׁ אֲחוֹתוֹ, דְּאִיתְּמַר: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אֲחוֹתוֹ — רַב אָמַר: מָעוֹת חוֹזְרִין, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מָעוֹת מַתָּנָה.

a2.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי חָזֵית דְּקָנְסִינַן לֵיהּ לְלוֹקֵחַ? נִקְנְסֵיהּ לְמוֹכֵר!

a3.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו עַכְבְּרָא גַּנָּב, אֶלָּא חוֹרָא גַּנָּב. אִי לָאו עַכְבְּרָא, חוֹרָא מְנָא לֵיהּ? מִסְתַּבְּרָא, הֵיכָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ לְאִיסּוּרָא קָנְסִינַן.

a4.he: הָיְתָה שְׁנַת שִׁדָּפוֹן כּוּ׳. הַשְׁתָּא הוֹבִירָהּ עוֹלָה לוֹ, נָרָהּ מִיבַּעְיָא?

a5.he: נָרָהּ אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ — סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא, אָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ: הַב לֵיהּ דְּמֵיהּ וְלִיסַּק, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a6.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מְכָרָהּ לוֹ כּוּ׳. תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם מְכָרָהּ לוֹ לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מְלֵיאָה פֵּירוֹת, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר לוֹ: ״הַנַּח לְפָנַי כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהִנַּחְתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ״? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי תְּבוּאוֹת יִמְכׇּר לָךְ״, פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם אוֹכֵל שָׁלֹשׁ תְּבוּאוֹת בִּשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים.

a7.he: מַתְנִי׳ מְכָרָהּ לָרִאשׁוֹן בְּמָנֶה, וּמָכַר רִאשׁוֹן לַשֵּׁנִי בְּמָאתַיִם, אֵינוֹ מְחַשֵּׁב אֶלָּא עִם הָרִאשׁוֹן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר מָכַר לוֹ״.

a8.he: מְכָרָהּ לָרִאשׁוֹן בְּמָאתַיִם, וּמָכַר הָרִאשׁוֹן לַשֵּׁנִי בְּמָנֶה — אֵינוֹ מְחַשֵּׁב אֶלָּא עִם הָאַחֲרוֹן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְחִשַּׁב אֶת שְׁנֵי מִמְכָּרוֹ וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת הָעוֹדֵף לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר מָכַר לוֹ״, לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹכוֹ.

a9.he: לֹא יִמְכּוֹר בְּרָחוֹק וְיִגְאַל בְּקָרוֹב, בְּרָעָה וְיִגְאַל בְּיָפָה, וְלֹא יִלְוֶה וְיִגְאַל, וְלֹא יִגְאַל לַחֲצָאִין, וּבַהֶקְדֵּשׁ מוּתָּר בְּכוּלָּן. זֶה חוֹמֶר בַּהֶדְיוֹט מִבַּהֶקְדֵּשׁ.

a10.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְכָרָהּ לָרִאשׁוֹן בְּמָנֶה, וּמְכָרָהּ רִאשׁוֹן לַשֵּׁנִי בְּמָאתַיִם, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחַשֵּׁב אֶלָּא עִם הָרִאשׁוֹן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״[לָאִישׁ] אֲשֶׁר מָכַר לוֹ״.

a11.he: מְכָרָהּ לָרִאשׁוֹן בְּמָאתַיִם, וּמָכַר הָרִאשׁוֹן לַשֵּׁנִי בְּמָנֶה, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא עִם הַשֵּׁנִי? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לָאִישׁ [לָאִישׁ] אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹכוֹ״, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי.

a12.he: רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מְכָרָהּ לוֹ בְּמָנֶה, וְהִשְׁבִּיחָהּ וְעָמְדָה עַל מָאתַיִם, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחַשֵּׁב אֶלָּא בְּמָנֶה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת הָעוֹדֵף״ — הָעוֹדֵף שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ.

a13.he: מְכָרָהּ לוֹ בְּמָאתַיִם, וְהִכְסִיפָה וְעָמְדָה עַל מָנֶה, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא בְּמָנֶה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת הָעוֹדֵף״ — הָעוֹדֵף שֶׁבַּקַּרְקַע.

a16.he: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּגָמַר ״גְּאוּלָּה״ ״גְּאוּלָּה״ מֵעֶבֶד עִבְרִי.

a17.he: וְהָתָם מְנָלַן? דְּתַנְיָא: נִמְכַּר בְּמָנֶה, וְהִשְׁבִּיחַ וְעָמַד עַל מָאתַיִם, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא מִמָּנֶה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ״.

a18.he: נִמְכַּר בְּמָאתַיִם, וְהִכְסִיף וְעָמַד עַל מָנֶה, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא מִמָּנֶה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כְּפִי שָׁנָיו״.

a19.he: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא עֶבֶד עִבְרִי הַנִּמְכָּר לְגוֹי, שֶׁנִּגְאָל וְיָדוֹ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, נִמְכָּר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״ לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה.

b1.he: הֲרֵינִי כְּבֶן עַזַּאי בְּשׁוּקֵי טְבֶרְיָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְאַבָּיֵי: אִיכָּא לְמִידְרְשִׁינְהוּ לְקוּלָּא, וְאִיכָּא לְמִידְרְשִׁינְהוּ לְחוּמְרָא, מִמַּאי דִּלְקוּלָּא? אֵימָא לְחוּמְרָא!

b2.he: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּיךְ, מִדְּאַקֵּיל רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּיהּ, דְּתַנְיָא: ״כִּי טוֹב לוֹ עִמָּךְ״ — עִמָּךְ בַּמַּאֲכָל, עִמְּךָ בַּמִּשְׁתֶּה, שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא אוֹכֵל פַּת נְקִיָּה וְהוּא אוֹכֵל פַּת קִיבָּר, אַתָּה שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן יָשָׁן וְהוּא שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן חָדָשׁ, אַתָּה יָשֵׁן עַל גַּבֵּי מוֹכִין וְהוּא יָשֵׁן עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע; מִיכָּן אָמְרוּ: הַקּוֹנֶה עֶבֶד עִבְרִי כְּקוֹנֶה אָדוֹן לְעַצְמוֹ.

b3.he: אַדְּרַבָּה, נַחְמִיר עֲלֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא! דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: ״בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה קָשֶׁה אֲבָקָהּ שֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית״.

b4.he: אָדָם נוֹשֵׂא וְנוֹתֵן בְּפֵירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית, לְסוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת מִטַּלְטְלָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל הַזֹּאת תָּשׁוּבוּ אִישׁ אֶל אֲחוּזָּתוֹ״, וּכְתִיב: ״וְכִי תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ אוֹ קָנֹה מִיַּד עֲמִיתֶךָ״, דָּבָר הַנִּקְנֶה מִיָּד לְיָד.

b5.he: לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ — לַסּוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת שְׂדוֹתָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכִי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ וּמָכַר מֵאֲחֻזָּתוֹ״.

b6.he: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת בֵּיתוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יִמְכּוֹר בֵּית מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה״. מַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם דְּקָאָמַר ״לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ״, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּקָאָמַר ״לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ״? כִּדְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבַר אָדָם עֲבֵירָה וְשָׁנָה בָּהּ, הוּתְּרָה לוֹ.

b7.he: הוּתְּרָה לוֹ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ?! אֶלָּא אֵימָא: נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר.

b8.he: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף שֶׁלֹּוֶה בְּרִבִּית, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכִי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ וְגוֹ׳״, וּכְתִיב: ״אַל תִּקַּח מֵאִתּוֹ נֶשֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּית״.

b9.he: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — עַד שֶׁמּוֹכֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכִי יִמְכּוֹר אִישׁ [אֶת] בִּתּוֹ לְאָמָה״, וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּבִתּוֹ בְּהַאי עִנְיָנָא לֵיתַהּ, נִיחָא לְאִינִישׁ דְּלִיזַבֵּין בְּרַתֵּיה וְלָא לֵיזִיף בְּרִיבִּיתָא, דְּאִילּוּ הָתָם מְיגָרְעָא וְאָזְלָא, וְאִילּוּ הָכָא קָא מוֹסְפָא וְאָזְלָא.

b10.he: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף שֶׁמּוֹכֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ וְנִמְכַּר לָךְ״; לֹא לָךְ אֶלָּא לְגֵר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לְגֵר״, וְלֹא לְגֵר צֶדֶק אֶלָּא לְגֵר תּוֹשָׁב, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לְגֵר תּוֹשָׁב״.

b11.he: ״מִשְׁפַּחַת גֵּר״ — זֶה הַגּוֹי. כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״אוֹ לְעֵקֶר מִשְׁפַּחַת גֵּר״ — זֶה הַנִּמְכָּר וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְשָׁרֵת לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה עַצְמָהּ.

b12.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא אַהְדְּרֵיהּ קְרָא, וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: הוֹאִיל וְהָלַךְ וּמָכַר עַצְמוֹ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, אֶידְחֶה אֶבֶן אַחֵר הַנּוֹפֵל? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״גְּאוּלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לּוֹ וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״. אֵימָא: גְּאוּלָּה תִּהְיֶה לוֹ — דְּלָא לִיטַּמַּע בַּגּוֹיִם, וּלְעוֹלָם לְעִנְיַן פִּדְיוֹנוֹ נַחְמִיר!

b13.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כְּתִיב ״אִם עוֹד רַבּוֹת בַּשָּׁנִים״, וּכְתִיב ״אִם מְעַט נִשְׁאַר בַּשָּׁנִים״.

b14.he: וְכִי יֵשׁ שָׁנִים מְרוּבּוֹת וְיֵשׁ שָׁנִים מוּעָטוֹת? אֶלָּא: נִתְרַבָּה כַּסְפּוֹ — ״מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ״, נִתְמַעֵט כַּסְפּוֹ — ״כְּפִי שָׁנָיו״.

b15.he: וְאֵימָא: הֵיכָא דַּעֲבַד תַּרְתֵּי וּפָיְישִׁי אַרְבְּעֵי — לִיתֵּב לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע ״מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ״, וְהֵיכָא דַּעֲבַד אַרְבַּע וּפָיְישִׁי תַּרְתֵּי — לִיתֵּב לֵיהּ תַּרְתֵּי ״כְּפִי שָׁנָיו״!

b16.he: אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב ״אִם עוֹד רַבּוֹת שָׁנִים״, מַאי ״בַּשָּׁנִים״? נִתְרַבָּה כַּסְפּוֹ בַּשָּׁנִים — מִ״כֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ״, נִתְמַעֵט כַּסְפּוֹ בַּשָּׁנִים — ״כְּפִי שָׁנָיו״. אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: דַּרְשִׁינְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן לְהָנֵי קְרָאֵי כְּסִינַי.

b17.he: לֹא יִמְכּוֹר בְּרָחוֹק כּוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְהִשִּׂיגָה יָדוֹ״ — יַד עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יִלְוֶה וְיִגְאַל.

b18.he: ״וּמָצָא״ — פְּרָט לְמָצוּי, שֶׁלֹּא יִמְכּוֹר בְּרָחוֹק וְיִגְאוֹל בְּקָרוֹב, בְּרַע וְיִגְאוֹל בְּיָפֶה; ״כְּדֵי גְאוּלָּתוֹ״ — כְּדֵי גְאוּלָּה הוּא גּוֹאֵל, וְאֵינוֹ גּוֹאֵל לַחֲצָאִין.

b19.he: לְמֵימְרָא דְּ״מָצָא״ הַשְׁתָּא מַשְׁמַע? וּרְמִינְהוּ: ״וּמָצָא״ — פְּרָט לְמַמְצִיא עַצְמוֹ, מִיכָּן אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: אִם מִשֶּׁיָּצְאָה אֶבֶן מִתַּחַת יָדוֹ, הוֹצִיא הַלָּה אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ וְקִיבְּלָהּ — פָּטוּר; אַלְמָא ״מָצָא״ מִידֵי דְּאִיתֵיהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא מַשְׁמַע!

b20.he: אָמַר רָבָא: הָכָא מֵעִנְיָנָא דִקְרָא, וְהָכָא מֵעִנְיָנָא דִקְרָא. הָכָא דּוּמְיָא דְּ״הִשִּׂיגָה יָדוֹ״, מָה ״הִשִּׂיגָה יָדוֹ״ דְּהַשְׁתָּא, אַף ״מָצָא״ נָמֵי דְּהַשְׁתָּא. וְהָכָא דּוּמְיָא דְּ״יַעַר״, מָה יַעַר מִילְּתָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא, אַף ״מָצָא״ מִילְּתָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא.

b21.he: וּבְהֶקְדֵּשׁ כּוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְאִם גָּאֹל יִגְאַל״ — מְלַמֵּד שֶׁלֹּוֶה וְגוֹאֵל, וְגוֹאֵל לַחֲצָאִין.

b22.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מָה טַעַם? לְפִי שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּמוֹכֵר שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה שֶׁיִּפָּה כֹּחוֹ, שֶׁאִם הִגִּיעַ יוֹבֵל וְלֹא נִגְאֲלָה חוֹזֶרֶת לַבְּעָלִים בַּיּוֹבֵל — הוֹרַע כֹּחוֹ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹוֶה וְגוֹאֵל, וְאֵינוֹ גּוֹאֵל לַחֲצָאִין.

b23.he: אֲבָל מַקְדִּישׁ שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, הוֹאִיל שֶׁהוֹרַע כֹּחוֹ, שֶׁאִם הִגִּיעַ יוֹבֵל וְלֹא נִגְאֲלָה יוֹצָא לַכֹּהֲנִים, יִפָּה כֹּחוֹ שֶׁלֹּוֶה וְגוֹאֵל וְגוֹאֵל לַחֲצָאִין.

messages.text: Continued from 29b: Rav Anan learned two halakhot from Shmuel, about a field sold in the Jubilee Year and a slave sold to gentiles or outside Eretz Yisrael, and that in one the sale is retracted and in the other it is not, but he did not know which. Rav Yosef resolved it from a baraita: a slave sold to a Jew outside Eretz Yisrael goes free but requires a bill of manumission from his second master, so there the sale stands, and Shmuel’s field “is not sold” and the money is returned.
Gemara

And Rav Anan did not resolve his dilemma from the baraita, as he did not learn this baraita. And he could not resolve it from the statement of Shmuel itself, that the sale of a field during the Jubilee Year is ineffective, as the meaning of Shmuel’s statement is unclear.

notes.he: דהוה מספקא ליה בהי הדרי ובהי לא הדרי הך ברייתא דצריך גט שיחרור לא הוה שמיעא ליה ומהא דאמר שמואל אינה מכורה לא הוה מצי למשמע מידי דממאי דאינה מכורה ומעות חוזרין דלמא מעות שנתן לוקח למוכר מתנה הן ביד מוכר ואיכא בין רב לשמואל הך דפרישית לעיל:
notes.en: And Rav Anan: who was uncertain in which case the sale is retracted and in which it is not. He had not heard that baraita, which says that a bill of manumission is required; and from what Shmuel said, “it is not sold,” he could not learn anything, for from where [do we know] that “it is not sold” means the money is returned? Perhaps the money the buyer gave the seller is a gift in the seller’s hand. And the difference between Rav and Shmuel is what I explained above.

notes.he: [הא ברייתא דצריך גט שחרור מרבו שני לא שמיעא ליה:
notes.en: This baraita, that he requires a bill of manumission from his second master, he had not heard.

messages.text: From where can one infer that Shmuel means that the field is not sold and the money is returned? Perhaps he means that the field is not sold and the money is considered a gift, just as it is considered a gift in his opinion in the case of one who betroths his sister. As it was stated:

notes.dh: דלמא אינה מכורה ומעות מתנה מידי דהוה אמקדש אחותו
notes.he: ומיהו לפי האמת שהוכחנו דמעות חוזרים אמרי' דלא דמי למקדש אחותו לפי שאדם יודע שאין קדושין תופסין באחותו וגמר ונתן לשם מתנה אבל במוכר שדהו בשנת היובל אין העולם בקיאין בכך ולא גמר לשום מתנה:
notes.en: Perhaps it is not sold and the money is a gift, just as with one who betroths his sister: However, according to the truth, which we have proven, that the money is returned, we say that it is not like one who betroths his sister. For a person knows that betrothal does not take effect with his sister, and resolves to give it as a gift; but with one who sells his field in the Jubilee Year, people are not expert in this, and he did not resolve [to give it] as a gift.

notes.he: (דממאי דאינה מכורה ומעות חוזרין דלמא):
notes.en: (For from where [do we know] that it is not sold and the money is returned? Perhaps…)

notes.he: מדשמואל נמי ליכא למשמע דהדרי זביני דממאי דאינה מכורה ומעות חוזרין דלמא אינה מכורה ומעות מתנה דלא הדרי. מידי דהוה אמקדש אחותו דרב אמר מעות חוזרין דאין קדושין תופסין באחותו:
notes.en: From Shmuel’s statement too one cannot learn that the sale is retracted, for from where [do we know] that “it is not sold” means the money is returned? Perhaps it is not sold and the money is a gift, which is not returned, just as with one who betroths his sister, where Rav says the money is returned, since betrothal does not take effect with his sister.

messages.text: The money with which the brother betrothed his sister is returned, as he knew that the betrothal was invalid and merely intended to deposit the money with her for safekeeping.
messages.lead: With regard to one who betroths his sister, a betrothal that is invalid,

notes.he: דאדם יודע שאין קדושין תופסין באחותו וגמר ונתן לשם פקדון ולשמואל גמר ונתן לשם מתנה:
notes.en: And the money is returned: for a person knows that betrothal does not take effect with his sister, so he resolved to give it as a deposit; and according to Shmuel, he resolved to give it as a gift.

messages.text: It is assumed that he wished to give her the money as a gift.

notes.he: דאדם יודע שאין קדושין תופסין באחותו וגמר ונתן לה לשום מתנה. [ואי קשיא] השתא כיון דאמרת לשמואל דמעות מתנה דלא הדרי ללוקח זוזי א"כ היינו דרב ומאי בינייהו]. איכא בינייהו אי שמיט לוקח ואכיל פירי לרב דאמר מכורה לא משלם פירי לשמואל דאמר אינה מכורה משלם פירי:
notes.en: And Shmuel says the money is a gift: for a person knows that betrothal does not take effect with his sister, and he resolved to give it to her as a gift. [And if you ask:] Now, since you said that according to Shmuel the money is a gift, which is not returned to the buyer, then this is Rav’s view; what is the difference between them? The difference between them is where the buyer seized [the field] and ate produce: according to Rav, who said it is sold, he does not pay for the produce; according to Shmuel, who said it is not sold, he pays for the produce.

messages.text: Back to the baraita cited on 29b: one who sells his slave to a Jew outside Eretz Yisrael, the buyer must free the slave, and his money is not refunded.

@Rav Yosef What did you see to say, that we penalize the buyer and he loses his money? Let us penalize the seller and require him to refund the money he received, so that he loses both the money and the slave.

notes.he: גבי מוכר עבדו בחוצה לארץ דאמרי' לא הדרי זביני ויוצא עבד לחירות ומפסיד לוקח:
notes.en: That you penalize the buyer: in the case of one who sells his slave outside the Land, where we say that the sale is not retracted, and the slave goes free and the buyer loses.

notes.he: שיהו מעות חוזרין ויוציאו מוכר לחירות:
notes.en: Let us penalize the seller: so that the money is returned and the seller sets him free.

notes.he: מאי חזית דקנסינן ליה ללוקח:
notes.en: What did you see that we penalize the buyer?

notes.he: שקנאו בחוצה לארץ שמניחו לחירות ומאבד מעותיו:
notes.en: Who acquired him outside the Land: that he must set him free and lose his money.

notes.he: כל שמכרו לחוצה לארץ:
notes.en: Let us penalize the seller: anyone who sold him [to a buyer] outside the Land.

messages.text: It is not the mouse that steals; rather, it is the hole that steals, as a mouse cannot steal any item unless he has a hole in which to hide it. In other words, the seller could not have sold his slave outside of Eretz Yisrael had the buyer been unwilling to purchase the slave.

notes.he: עכבר הגונב ומניח בחוץ אם לא היה לו חור להניח בו לא היה גונב הלכך חורא גנבא וקא גניב ליה ה"נ אם לא היה מוצא לוקח לא היה מוכרו:
notes.en: It is not the mouse that steals: a mouse that steals and puts the item away; had it no hole in which to put it, it would not steal. Therefore it is the hole that steals. So too here: had he not found a buyer, he would not have sold him.

notes.he: כלומר אותו שקונה גורם לזה שמוציאו לחוצה לארץ ומוכרו:
notes.en: The hole steals: that is, the one who buys causes this one to take him out of the Land and sell him.

messages.text: The opposite is also true, namely that if not for the mouse, from where would the hole obtain the stolen item? Had the seller refused to sell his slave, the buyer could not have purchased him and taken him out of Eretz Yisrael.
messages.quote: it is the hole that steals

notes.he: החור מאין לו הגניבה:
notes.en: The hole, from where would it have it: from where would the hole have the stolen item?

messages.text: Although both parties are at fault, it stands to reason that we apply the penalty wherever the subject of the prohibition is currently located. Since the buyer is now in possession of the slave, he is the one who is penalized.

notes.he: דהיינו לוקח שהעבד אצלו:
notes.en: Where the prohibited item is: that is, the buyer, with whom the slave is.

notes.he: שהוא ביד הלוקח ליה קנסינן הלכך קנסינן ליה ללוקח:
notes.en: Where the prohibited item is: he is in the buyer’s hand, so we penalize him; therefore we penalize the buyer.

messages.text: If one of the two years after the sale was a year of blight, the buyer is entitled to an additional year’s crops. If the buyer plowed the field but did not sow it, or if he left it fallow, that year counts as part of his tally, as it was fit to produce a crop.

Now that it was taught that if the buyer left his field fallow that year counts as part of his tally, even though he did not cultivate the field at all, is it necessary for the mishna to teach that the year counts as part of his tally if he plowed the field but did not sow it?
messages.quote: If the buyer plowed the field but did not sow it, or if he left it fallow

notes.he: דעולה לו מן המנין דהא כבר עבד בה מידי עבודה:
notes.en: Is it necessary [to state] that he plowed: that it counts for him, since he already did some work in it?

messages.text: It was necessary to teach the case of a buyer who plowed the field but did not sow it, as it might enter your mind to say that we say to the seller: Give the monetary value of the enhancement of the field to the buyer, and then he will leave the field.

notes.he: פי' דמי הניר קמ"ל]:
notes.en: [Give him its value: meaning, the value of the plowing. It teaches us that this is not so.]

notes.he: דעולה לו דסד"א כיון דנרה ולא זרעה ולא נהנה (זה) ממנה הלוקח כלום דאמרינן ליה למוכר בשעה שפודה כיון שטרח (זה) בה שנרה והשביחה ולא נהנה ממנה הב ליה ללוקח דמי כרביה שחרשה והשביחה:
notes.en: Plowed was necessary: that it counts for him. For you might have said: since he plowed and did not sow, and the buyer derived no benefit from it, we say to the seller when he redeems: since this one troubled himself with it, plowing and improving it, and had no benefit from it, give the buyer the value of his improvement, since he plowed and improved it.

notes.he: כלומר (והחזר) [כשיחזיר] לו העודף הדמים שכנגד השנים שיש עוד עד היובל ודמי חרישתו ודמים שהשביחו ואח"כ יסתלק ויצא (לו) חוץ (מן) לשדה:
notes.en: And let him leave: that is, when he returns to him the remainder of the money for the years still left until the Jubilee, and the value of his plowing and of the improvement he made, and afterward he withdraws and goes out of the field.

messages.text: The mishna therefore teaches us that the seller does not have to pay him that amount.

notes.he: דלא יהיב ליה המוכר מידי שכר חרישה דאמר ליה כיון שהיתה ברשותך שהיתה יכול לזורעה וליקח תבואתה ולא עבדת את הוא דאפסדת נפשך וינכה לו המוכר שיגרע לו דמי אותן שני שנים כאילו היו זרועות ואכל הלוקח תבואתן:
notes.en: It teaches us: that the seller gives him nothing for the plowing, for he says to him: Since it was in your possession, and you could have sown it and taken its crop, and you did not, you are the one who caused yourself a loss. And the seller deducts the value of those two years as if they had been sown and the buyer had eaten their crop.

messages.text: If the owner of the field sold it to the buyer before Rosh HaShana and the field was full of produce, and the owner redeems the field after two years, the buyer consumes three crops of the field’s produce in two years.

From where is it derived that if the owner of the field sold it to the buyer before Rosh HaShana full of produce, that the seller should not say to the buyer when he redeems the field after two years: Leave the field for me full of produce in the manner that I left it for you?
messages.lead: With regard to this halakha it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: the buyer consumes three crops of the field’s produce in two years

notes.he: מוכר הבא לפדותה לסוף שתי שנים הנח לפני מליאה פירות כדרך שהנחתי לפניך כשמכרתי לך:
notes.en: That he should not say: the seller, who comes to redeem it at the end of two years, [should not say]: Leave it before me full of produce, the way I left it before you when I sold it to you.

notes.he: [מנין שלא יאמר לו המוכר ללוקח הנח לפני השדה מליאה פירות בסוף שני שנים שלא תיטול פירותיה כדרך שהנחתיה מליאה לפניך בשעה שמכרתיה לך:
notes.en: From where [do we know] that the seller should not say to the buyer: Leave the field before me full of produce at the end of the two years, so that you do not take its produce, the way I left it before you full when I sold it to you?

messages.text: The verse states: “According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you” (Leviticus 25:15), indicating that the payment is calculated according to the number of years, not according to the number of crops. Consequently, sometimes a person consumes three crops in two years.

verse.he: בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל תִּקְנֶה מֵאֵת עֲמִיתֶךָ בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי־תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר־לָךְ׃
verse.en: In buying from your neighbor, you shall deduct only for the number of years since the jubilee; and in selling to you, you shall be charged only for the remaining crop years:

notes.he: משמע כל תבואות שבשתי שנים מדהוה ליה למיכתב מספר שנים או מספר תבואות דהוי משמע שתי תבואות:
notes.en: According to the number of years of the crops: this implies all the crops of two years, since [otherwise] it could have written “the number of years” or “the number of crops,” which would have implied two crops.

notes.dh: ת"ל מספר שני תבואות ימכר לך
notes.he: כלומר כל התבואות שאפשר להיות בה משעת מכירה עד סוף שני שנים הן מכורות והן של לוקח:
notes.en: The verse states: “According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you”: that is, all the crops that can be in it from the time of the sale to the end of two years are sold and belong to the buyer.

messages.text: Mishna

When the Jubilee Year is in effect, one may sell a field only until the Jubilee Year, at which point the field returns to its original owner. If the owner redeems the field before the Jubilee Year, the payment per annum is calculated by dividing the sale price by the number of years from the sale until the Jubilee Year. The owner returns the per annum payment multiplied by the number of years remaining until the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: המוכר כשבא לגאלה אלא עם הראשון ומחשב כמה שנים היו משמכרה לו עד שנת היובל ומחשב כמה מגיע מן המנה לכל שנה ולפי אותו חשבון ינכה לו לוקח לכל שנה ושנה שאכלה והמותר יחזיר לו:
notes.en: Mishna. He calculates only: the seller, when he comes to redeem it, [calculates] only with the first. He calculates how many years there were from when he sold it to him until the Jubilee Year, and calculates how much of the maneh falls to each year; and according to that calculation the buyer deducts for him for each year in which he ate [its produce], and he returns the rest to him.

notes.he: מכרה שדהו לראשון במנה וחזר הלוקח ראשון ומכרה לשני במאתים כשהוא פודה אותה המוכר שהוא בעל השדה]:
notes.en: He sold his field to the first for a maneh, and the first buyer then sold it to the second for two hundred; when the seller, who is the owner of the field, redeems it:

messages.text: If the owner of a field sold it to the first buyer for one hundred dinars and the first buyer then sold it to the second buyer for two hundred dinars, when the original owner redeems the field he calculates the payment only according to the price that he set with the first buyer, as it is stated: “And he calculates the years of its sale, and he returns the remainder to the man to whom he sold it” (Leviticus 25:27).

verse.he: וְחִשַּׁב אֶת־שְׁנֵי מִמְכָּרוֹ וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת־הָעֹדֵף לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר מָכַר־לוֹ וְשָׁב לַאֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: the years since its sale shall be computed and the difference shall be refunded to the party to whom it was sold, so that [the seller] returns to their holding.

notes.he: והשיב את העודף לאיש וגו' בגואל שדה ממכרו כתיב:
notes.en: [To the man] to whom he sold it: “And he returns the remainder to the man…” is written of one who redeems a field that he sold.

notes.he: כדכתיב וחשב את שני ממכרו והשיב את העודף:
notes.en: He calculates only: as it is written: “And he calculates the years of its sale and returns the remainder.”

notes.he: למי שמכרה לו כדי להקל על הגואל ויפסיד (זה) הלוקח שני מנה אחד וכן מכרה לראשון במאתים (וזה) [וחזר] הלוקח ומכרה לשני במנה אינו מחשב אותו שהיה בעל השדה כשבא לגאול אלא עם הלוקח אחרון:
notes.en: Only with the first: to whom he sold it, so as to make it easier for the redeemer, and the second buyer loses one maneh. And likewise, if he sold it to the first for two hundred and the buyer then sold it to the second for a maneh, the one who was owner of the field, when he comes to redeem it, calculates only with the last buyer.

messages.text: If the owner of a field sold it to the first buyer for two hundred dinars and the first buyer then sold it to the second buyer for one hundred dinars, when the original owner redeems the field, he calculates the payment only according to the price that was paid by the last buyer, as it is stated: “And he calculates the years of its sale, and he returns the remainder to the man to whom he sold it.” The superfluous term “to the man” indicates that the verse is referring to the man who is currently in possession of the field.

notes.he: ובגמ' פריך מנלן דדרשינן לקולא לידרוש לחומרא:
notes.en: To the man who is in it: and in the Gemara it asks: From where do we know that we expound it as a leniency? Let us expound it as a stringency.

notes.he: [לאיש שבתוכה] כלומר לאותו שתופס השדה והאי דדרשינן לקרא הכי מפני שאנו רוצים להקל על הגואל. אבל בענין זה נחמיר על הגואל:
notes.en: As it is stated: “And he returns the remainder to the man”: [to the man who is in it], that is, to the one who holds the field. We expound the verse this way because we wish to make it easier for the redeemer; but in that [other] way we would be stringent with the redeemer.

messages.text: One may not sell his ancestral field that is located in a distant area and redeem with the proceeds a field that he sold in a nearby area. Likewise, he may not sell a low-quality field and redeem with the proceeds a high-quality field. And he may not borrow money and redeem the field, nor may he redeem the field incrementally, half now and half at a later date.

notes.he: שיש לו כדי לגאול זו שהיא קרובה לו. בגמרא מפרש מנלן:
notes.en: He may not sell a distant field: which he has, in order to redeem this one, which is near him. The Gemara explains from where we know this.

notes.he: מעות כדי לגאלה:
notes.en: And he may not borrow: money in order to redeem it.

notes.he: ה"ה איפכא דלא אלא אורחא דמילתא נקט:
notes.en: He may not sell [a field] far away and redeem [one] nearby: the same is true in reverse; it simply states the usual way of things.

notes.he: כלומר שאם יש לו לגואל שדה אחת ברחוק ממנו אינו רשאי למכור אותו כדי לגאול באותן דמים שדה זו שהיא בקרוב לו שמכרה לשני תבואות ומפרשינן בגמרא טעמא מאי. וכן לא ימכור ברע שדה רעה שיש לו כדי לגאול באותן דמים שדה יפה לו שמכרה לשני תבואות. וכן אינו רשאי ללות מעות מאחר כדי לגאול שדה זו וכן אינו רשאי לגואלה בחצאין אא"כ יתנו לו הדמים כולן בבת אחת]:
notes.en: That he may not sell [a field] far away [and redeem one nearby: that is, if the redeemer has a field far from him, he is not permitted to sell it in order to redeem with that money this field, which is near him, which he sold for two crop-years; and in the Gemara we explain the reason. And likewise he may not sell a bad field that he has in order to redeem with that money a good field of his that he sold for two crop-years. And likewise he is not permitted to borrow money from another to redeem this field, and he is not permitted to redeem it by halves, unless he gives all the money at once.]

messages.text: But with regard to redeeming a field from the Temple treasury, it is permitted to redeem the field in any of these ways. This is a halakha where greater stringency applies with regard to redeeming a field from an ordinary individual than with regard to redeeming it from the Temple treasury.

notes.he: המקדיש שדהו מותר למכור שדה אחרת או ללות כדי לגאלה וגואל לחצאין אם אינו מספיק לגאול את כולה יגאל חציה ולכשיוכל יגאלנה כולה:
notes.en: Permitted in all of them: one who consecrates his field is permitted to sell another field, or to borrow, in order to redeem it. And he redeems by halves: if he does not have enough to redeem all of it, he redeems half of it, and when he is able, he redeems all of it.

notes.he: המקדיש שדהו בשעת היובל מותר בכולן למכור ברחוק ולגאול בקרוב [ולמכור] ברע. [ולגאול ביפה] [לוה וגואל] וגואל לחצאין ואע"ג דאמרי' לעיל אם אמר הריני נותן דבר שנה בשנה אין שומעין לו ה"מ דאין שומעין לו [לגואלה] ליתן סלע ופונדיון לכל שנה אבל אם נותן החצי (פונדיון) [ביחד] ולבסוף חצי האחר מותר והיינו דקאמר ובהקדש מותר לגאול לחצאין:
notes.en: And with consecrated property: one who consecrates his field when the Jubilee is in effect is permitted in all of them: to sell a distant field and redeem a near one, [to sell] a bad one [and redeem a good one], [to borrow and redeem], and to redeem by halves. And although we said above that if he says, “I will give the amount year by year,” we do not listen to him, that is only that we do not listen to him [to redeem it] by giving a sela and a pundeyon each year; but if he gives half [together] and later the other half, it is permitted. And this is what it says: with consecrated property it is permitted to redeem by halves.

messages.text: Gemara

Consider the case where the owner of a field sold it to the first buyer for one hundred dinars and the first buyer then sold it to the second buyer for two hundred dinars. From where is it derived that when the original owner redeems the field, he calculates the payment only according to the price that he set with the first buyer? The verse states: “And he calculates the years of its sale, and he returns the remainder to the man to whom he sold it” (Leviticus 25:27).
messages.quote: he calculates the payment only according to the price that he set with the first buyer

messages.text: Now consider the case where the owner of a field sold it to the first buyer for two hundred dinars and the first buyer then sold it to the second buyer for one hundred dinars. From where is it derived that when the original owner redeems the field, the payment is calculated only according to the price that was paid by the second buyer? The verse states: “And he returns the remainder to the man to whom he sold it.” The superfluous term “to the man” indicates that the verse is referring to the man who is currently in possession of the field. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

Consider the case where the owner of a field sold it to the buyer for one hundred dinars, and the field appreciated in value while in the buyer’s possession and its value stood at two hundred dinars. From where is it derived that when the seller redeems the field he calculates the payment only according to the one hundred dinars he originally received for the field? As it is stated: “And he returns the remainder to the man to whom he sold it,” that is, the seller returns only the remainder of the original payment that is in his possession.
messages.lead: The verse should be interpreted differently:

notes.he: מאליה:
notes.en: Gemara. And it appreciated: on its own.

notes.he: הנשאר בידו מן הדמים שקיבל לאחר שינכה לו הלוקח חשבון המגיע לכל שנה שאכלה:
notes.en: The remainder in his hand: what remains in his hand of the money he received, after the buyer deducts for him the amount due for each year in which he ate.

notes.he: כלומר העודף שביד המוכר שיש לו מן הדמים שנתן לו הלוקח [הוא מחזיר ללוקח] ולא משבח שהשביחה:
notes.en: The remainder in his hand: that is, the remainder in the seller’s hand of the money the buyer gave him [he returns to the buyer], and not the improvement by which it improved.

messages.text: Consider the case where the owner of a field sold it to the buyer for two hundred dinars, and the field depreciated in value while in the buyer’s possession and its value stood at one hundred dinars. From where is it derived that when the seller redeems the field, the payment is calculated only according to the one hundred dinars the field is currently worth? As it is stated: “And he returns the remainder to the man to whom he sold it,” i.e., he returns that which now remains of the value of the land.

notes.he: נתקלקלה ופחתו דמיה:
notes.en: Depreciated: it was spoiled and its value dropped.

notes.he: עודף שהקרקע שוה יותר על מה שמגיע לחשבון שמנכה לו הלוקח לשנים שאכלה דהאי עודף איכא למדרש להכי ולהכי:
notes.en: That is in the land: the remainder, what the land is worth beyond the amount due by the calculation the buyer deducts for him for the years in which he ate. For this word “remainder” can be expounded this way and that way.

notes.he: כלומר דאזלינן גבי (כהן) [גואל] לקולא:
notes.en: The remainder in the land: that is, for we go toward leniency with the [redeemer; the printed text reads “priest”].

messages.text: What is the practical difference between the opinions of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda?

notes.he: בין רבי לר' דוסתאי מ"מ בין למר בין למר לקולא אזלינן:
notes.en: What is the difference between them: between Rabbi and Rabbi Dostai, since in any case, according to both of them, we go toward leniency.

notes.he: [בין ר' לר' דוסתאי] דהא תרוויהו מקילין גבי גואל:
notes.en: What is the difference between them: [between Rabbi and Rabbi Dostai], since both of them are lenient with the redeemer?

messages.text: The practical difference between them is in a case where the field’s value was high at the time of the first sale, e.g., it was worth two hundred dinars, and when the field was sold a second time it had depreciated in value and was worth only one hundred dinars. And when the original owner came to redeem it, it again appreciated in value until it was worth two hundred dinars.

notes.he: שמכרה לו במאתים ומכרה ראשון לשני במנה ונתייקרה ביד השני ועמדה על מאתים. לרבי דאמר לאיש אשר בתוכה לא יהיב אלא מנה כמה דיהיב בה שני לר' דוסתאי יהיב מאתים דאי אמרת עודף שבידו הא מאתן שקיל מקמא ואי אמרת עודף שבקרקע הא מאתן שויא:
notes.en: Such as where it went up, went down and went up: he sold it to him for two hundred, and the first sold it to the second for a maneh, and it went up in value in the second’s hand and stood at two hundred. According to Rabbi, who said “to the man who is in it,” he gives only a maneh, as much as the second gave for it. According to Rabbi Dostai, he gives two hundred: for if you say “the remainder in his hand,” he took two hundred from the first; and if you say “the remainder in the land,” it is worth two hundred.

notes.he: ה"ה דהוה מצי למימר דאייקר וזל בלוקח אחד בלבד דאילו לרבי דלא דריש העודף בין לאיש אשר מכר בין לאיש אשר בתוכה צריך לגואלה כפי המכר דהיינו ביוקר ולרבי דוסתאי ברבי יהודה אזלינן בתר העלוי שבקרקע ונגאלת כפי העלוי אלא לפי דאיירי במתניתין בשני מוכרין ניחא ליה למינקט נמי איכא בינייהו בשני מוכרין:
notes.en: The difference between them is where it went up, went down and went up: it could equally have said “where it went up and went down” with only one buyer. For according to Rabbi, who does not expound “the remainder” [this way], but rather [expounds] “to the man to whom he sold it” and “to the man who is in it,” one must redeem it according to the sale, that is, at the high price; and according to Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yehuda [so Tosafot; the Gemara reads “ben Yehuda”], we go by the value of the land, and it is redeemed according to its value. But since the mishna speaks of two sellers, it preferred to state the difference between them with two sellers as well.

messages.text: According to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, the redemption payment is calculated according to the one hundred dinars paid by the second buyer for the field. According to Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda, it is calculated either according to the remainder of the original payment or according to that which now remains of the value of the land. Either way, it is calculated according to the remainder of two hundred dinars.

notes.he: כלומר שמכרה לו במאתים והוזלה [דהכסיפה] ובשעת פדיה הוקרה ושויא מאתים לר' דלא איירי בעודף שבידו ולא בעודף שבקרקע ולא בהכסיפה [לטעמיה] אם מכרה במאתים והוזלה [דהיינו שהכסיפה] וחזרה ועמדה במאתים [דהיינו שהוקרה] ואין שם אלא לוקח אחד אמרינן גואלה במאתים [דהיינו לאשר מכר לו ולר' דוסתאי דאזיל בתר עודף שבידו ועודף שבקרקע אזלינן נמי בתר קרקע דמחשב ליה בחשבון הזול:
notes.en: The difference between them is where it went up, went down and went up: that is, he sold it to him for two hundred and it went down [that is, it depreciated], and at the time of redemption it went up and was worth two hundred. According to Rabbi, who speaks neither of the remainder in his hand nor of the remainder in the land nor of depreciation, [by his reasoning,] if he sold it for two hundred and it went down [that is, depreciated] and then stood again at two hundred [that is, appreciated], and there is only one buyer, we say he redeems it for two hundred [that is, “to the man to whom he sold it”]. And according to Rabbi Dostai, who goes by the remainder in his hand and the remainder in the land, we also go by the land, so it is calculated for him at the lower value.

messages.caption: Redeeming a sold field: the mishna’s two buyers, Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda’s rise and fall in value, and the case where Rabbi and Rabbi Dostai differ.

messages.text: The aforementioned practical difference aside, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda agree that the verses are interpreted in a manner that benefits the original owner. And from where is it derived that the verses should be interpreted as a leniency for the seller? Perhaps they should be interpreted as a stringency for the seller.

notes.he: [ואית דאמר לר' דאזיל בתר קרקע הואיל ובשעת פדייה שוה כשעת מכר נותן לו מאתים כשעת המכר. למ"ה]. וממאי דלקולא אימא לחומרא. כלומר דקראי אפשר למידרשינהו [גבי גואל לקולא ואיכא למידרשינהו] לחומרא דאיכא למימר כי מכרה הראשון לשני במאתים מנין שאין מחשב אלא עם השני ת"ל לאיש אשר בתוכה והיינו חומרא וכי [מכרה] לראשון במאתים מנין שאין מחשב אלא עם הראשון ת"ל לאיש אשר מכר לו והיינו חומרא ומנ"ל דדרשינן להו לקולא:
notes.en: [And some say: according to Rabbi, who goes by the land, since at the time of redemption it is worth as much as at the time of sale, he gives him two hundred, as at the time of sale.] And from where [do we know] that it is for leniency? Say for stringency: that is, the verses can be expounded [as a leniency for the redeemer, and they can be expounded] as a stringency. For one could say: when the first sold it to the second for two hundred, from where [do we know] that he calculates only with the second? The verse states “to the man who is in it,” and that is a stringency. And when [he sold it] to the first for two hundred, from where [do we know] that he calculates only with the first? The verse states “to the man to whom he sold it,” and that is a stringency. So from where do we know to expound them as a leniency?

messages.text: Such a possibility should not enter your mind, as it is learned by means of a verbal analogy between the term “redemption” written in this context and “redemption” from the passage discussing a Hebrew slave that the Torah is lenient with regard to the redeemer.

notes.he: כתיב הכא (ויקרא כ״ה:כ״ו) ומצא כדי גאולתו וכתיב בעבד עברי (שם) גאולה תהיה לו:
notes.en: Redemption, redemption: it is written here (Leviticus 25:26), “and finds sufficient means for its redemption,” and it is written of a Hebrew slave (ibid. 25:48), “he shall have redemption.”

notes.he: [דגמר גאולה גאולה מעבד עברי כתוב כאן והשיג ידו ומצא כדי גאולתו וכתיב בעבד עברי לפיהן ישיב גאולתו:
notes.en: For he derives “redemption,” “redemption” from a Hebrew slave: it is written here, “And he prospers and finds sufficient means for its redemption,” and it is written of a Hebrew slave, “According to them he shall return the price of his redemption.”

messages.text: The verse states with regard to the redemption of a field: “And he prospers and finds sufficient means to redeem it” (Leviticus 25:26), and with regard to the redemption of a slave who was sold to a gentile, the verse states: “After he is sold he shall attain redemption” (Leviticus 25:48). Accordingly, just as the Torah is lenient with regard to the redemption of a Hebrew slave, so too the Torah is lenient with regard to redeeming a field.

verse.he: אַחֲרֵי נִמְכַּר גְּאֻלָּה תִּהְיֶה־לּוֹ אֶחָד מֵאֶחָיו יִגְאָלֶנּוּ׃
verse.en: [your kin] shall have the right of redemption even afterward. [Typically,] a brother shall do the redeeming,

messages.text: And there, in the case of a Hebrew slave, from where do we derive that the Torah is lenient with regard to his redemption? As it is taught in a baraita:

Consider the case of a Hebrew slave who was sold for one hundred dinars, and he appreciated in value during his term of servitude and his value stood at two hundred dinars. From where is it derived that if he redeems himself, the sum he pays for the remaining years of his service is calculated only according to the one hundred dinars for which he was originally sold? As it is stated: “If there are yet many years, according to them he shall return the price of his redemption from the money of his purchase” (Leviticus 25:51).

verse.he: אִם־עוֹד רַבּוֹת בַּשָּׁנִים לְפִיהֶן יָשִׁיב גְּאֻלָּתוֹ מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ׃
verse.en: If many years remain, [your kin] shall pay back for the redemption in proportion to the purchase price;

notes.he: כשבא לפדות עצמו מחשב כמה שנים משעה שנמכר (עד שנת היובל) ומחשב כמה מגיע מאותו מנה לכל שנה ושנה ואם עברו שתים או שלש שנים ינכה לו אדוניו לפי חשבון המגיע לכל שנה כדכתיב כימי שכיר יהיה עמו:
notes.en: Only from a maneh: when he comes to redeem himself, he calculates how many years [there are] from the time he was sold (until the Jubilee Year), and calculates how much of that maneh falls to each year; and if two or three years have passed, his master deducts for him according to the amount due for each year, as it is written: “According to the time of a hired worker shall he be with him.”

notes.he: מנין שאין מחשב אלא ממנה שהוא גורע נמי דמי שני עבודתו ונותן מותר דמי השנים שיש עד שנת השביעית שנאמר מכסף מקנתו דמחשב משעה שנמכר כפי שניו שהוא שוה עכשיו והני קראי משתעי בעבד עברי שנמכר לעובד כוכבים]:
notes.en: From the money of his purchase: from where [do we know] that he calculates only from a maneh, that he also deducts the value of the years of his service and gives the balance for the years remaining until the seventh year? As it is stated, “from the money of his purchase”: he calculates from the time he was sold. “According to his years”: what he is worth now. And these verses speak of a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile.

messages.text: Consider the case of a Hebrew slave who was sold for two hundred dinars, and he depreciated in value during his term and his value stood at one hundred dinars. From where is it derived that if he redeems himself, the sum he pays for the remaining years of his service is calculated only according to the one hundred dinars he is currently worth? As it is stated: “According to his years he shall return the price of his redemption” (Leviticus 25:52). The verse indicates that the sum is calculated according to the value of his remaining years of service.

verse.he: וְאִם־מְעַט נִשְׁאַר בַּשָּׁנִים עַד־שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְחִשַּׁב־לוֹ כְּפִי שָׁנָיו יָשִׁיב אֶת־גְּאֻלָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: and if few years remain until the jubilee year, so shall it be computed: payment shall be made for the redemption according to the years involved.

notes.he: משמע כפי שנים שעמד בהן כלומר לפי מה שהוא שוה באותה שעה:
notes.en: According to his years: this implies according to the years in which he stands, that is, according to what he is worth at that time.

messages.text: And I have derived only with regard to a Hebrew slave who was sold to a gentile, that he is redeemed and that he has the advantage, as the price of his redemption is always calculated according to the lesser value. From where is it derived that this halakha also applies in the case of a Hebrew slave who was sold to a Jew?

notes.he: דהאי קרא בנמכר לעובד כוכבים כתיב כדכתיב (שם) וכי תשיג יד גר ותושב וכו':
notes.en: I have only, etc.: for this verse is written about one sold to a gentile, as it is written (ibid.): “And if a stranger or settler becomes rich…”

messages.text: The verse states: “Hired worker,” “hired worker,” in order to derive a verbal analogy, indicating that this halakha applies both to a slave sold to a gentile and to one sold to a Jew. The verse states with regard to a slave sold to a gentile: “According to the time of a hired worker shall he be with him” (Leviticus 25:50), and with regard to a slave sold to a Jew, the verse states: “For double the hire of a hired worker he served you six years” (Deuteronomy 15:18).

verse.he: לֹא־יִקְשֶׁה בְעֵינֶךָ בְּשַׁלֵּחֲךָ אֹתוֹ חׇפְשִׁי מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי מִשְׁנֶה שְׂכַר שָׂכִיר עֲבָדְךָ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים וּבֵרַכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה׃ {פ}
verse.en: When you do set them free, do not feel aggrieved; for in the six years you have been given double the service of a hired worker. Moreover, the ETERNAL your God will bless you in all you do.

notes.he: כתיב הכא (שם) כימי שכיר יהיה עמו וכתיב בנמכר לישראל (דברים ט״ו:י״ח) כי משנה שכר שכיר עבדך וגו':
notes.en: Hired worker, hired worker: it is written here (ibid.), “According to the time of a hired worker shall he be with him,” and it is written of one sold to a Jew (Deuteronomy 15:18), “For double the hire of a hired worker he served you…”

notes.he: כתיב הכא בנמכר לישראל כשכיר כתושב יהיה עמך וכתיב הכא בנמכר לעובד כוכבים כשכיר שנה בשנה:
notes.en: Hired worker, hired worker, for a verbal analogy: it is written here, of one sold to a Jew, “As a hired worker, as a settler, he shall be with you,” and it is written here, of one sold to a gentile, “As a hired worker year by year.”

messages.text: The Gemara relates that Abaye said:
I am ready to answer any questions put to me like those of the intellectually sharp ben Azzai, who would regularly expound in the markets of Tiberias.

notes.he: משובח במקומי שאני דרשן ובקי כבן עזאי שהיה משתבח בשוקי טבריא כדתניא בבכורות בפ' תשיעי (דף נח.) בן עזאי אומר כל חכמי ישראל לפני כקליפת השום:
notes.en: I am: praiseworthy in my place, an expounder and expert like ben Azzai, who would praise himself in the markets of Tiberias, as it is taught in Bekhorot, in the ninth chapter (58a): Ben Azzai says: All the Sages of Israel are before me like the peel of garlic.

notes.he: שכשם שהוא היה חכם גדול דהיה עומד בשוק ואומר כל מי שרוצה לשואלני דבר הרני משיבו אף אני כן מי שירצה יבא וישאלני:
notes.en: I am like ben Azzai in the markets of Tiberias: just as he was a great Sage who would stand in the market and say, “Whoever wishes to ask me anything, I will answer him,” so too I: whoever wishes, let him come and ask me.

messages.text: The verses discussing the redemption of a Hebrew slave can be interpreted as a leniency for the slave, and they can also be interpreted as a stringency for him. From where is it derived that the verses should be interpreted as a leniency for the slave? Say that they should be interpreted as a stringency for him.
messages.lead: One of the Sages said to Abaye:
messages.quote: I am ready to answer any questions put to me

notes.he: הני קראי דעבד עברי:
notes.en: They can be expounded: these verses of the Hebrew slave.

notes.dh: [מכדי הני קראי דעבד עברי איכא למידרשינהו בין לקולא בין לחומרא]
notes.he: לחומרא דאיכא למימר כי השביח מנין שאין מחשב (אלא) במאתים ת"ל לפי שניו ואם הכסיף מנין שאין מחשב אלא במאתים ת"ל מכסף מקנתו והיינו לחומרא:
notes.en: [Now, these verses of a Hebrew slave can be expounded both as a leniency and as a stringency.] As a stringency: one could say, when he appreciated, from where [do we know] that he calculates only at two hundred? The verse states “according to his years.” And if he depreciated, from where [do we know] that he calculates only at two hundred? The verse states “from the money of his purchase.” And that is as a stringency.

messages.text: Such a possibility should not enter your mind, due to the fact that the Merciful One was explicitly lenient with regard to a slave. As it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: Say that they should be interpreted as a stringency for him

notes.he: שאין נוהג בו מנהג בזיון אקיל נמי בפדיונו:
notes.en: Since the Merciful One was lenient with him: that one may not treat him in a degrading manner, He was also lenient with his redemption.

messages.text: The verse states with regard to a Hebrew slave: “And it shall be, if he says to you I will not leave you…because he fares well with you” (Deuteronomy 15:16). The term “with you” indicates that the slave must be with you, i.e., treated as your equal, with regard to food, and with you with regard to drink.

verse.he: וְהָיָה כִּי־יֹאמַר אֵלֶיךָ לֹא אֵצֵא מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אֲהֵבְךָ וְאֶת־בֵּיתֶךָ כִּי־טוֹב לוֹ עִמָּךְ׃
verse.en: But should they say to you, “I do not want to leave you”—for they love you and your household and are happy with you—

notes.he: הכי איתא בכל הספרים ונראה דלא גרסינן הכי דאין זה כי אם סיפור דברים של העבד כי אהבך ואת ביתך כי טוב לו עמך ואין זה ציווי אלא גרס כדאיתא בסיפרי כתושב כשכיר יהיה עמך דהיינו ציווי:
notes.en: As it is taught: “Because he fares well with you”: so it appears in all the books, but it seems that we should not read it so, for this is only a narration of the slave’s words, “because he loves you and your house, because he fares well with you,” and it is not a command. Rather, read as it appears in the Sifrei: “As a hired worker, as a settler, he shall be with you” [Leviticus 25:40], which is a command.

messages.text: This means that you should not be eating fine bread while he eats inferior bread [kibbar], bread from coarse flour mixed with bran. Likewise, you should not drink old wine while he drinks inferior new wine. You should not sleep on bedding made from soft sheets while he sleeps on the ground.

notes.he: שגונדיי"ר:
notes.en: Kibbar: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

messages.text: From here the Sages stated: One who acquires a Hebrew slave is considered like one who acquires a master for himself, as he must ensure that the slave’s living conditions are equal to his own.

On the contrary, let us impose a stringency upon the slave, due to the statement of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina. As Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says in explanation of the juxtaposition of several passages in the Torah (Leviticus, chapter 25):
messages.lead: That Sage raised an objection to Abaye:

notes.he: דודאי לא בא לידי כך אלא מפני שהיה רשע ועושה סחורה בפירות שביעית:
notes.en: From [the statement of] Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina: for certainly he came to this only because he was wicked and traded in Sabbatical-Year produce.

messages.text: Come and see how severe is even the hint of violation of the prohibition of the Sabbatical Year, as the prohibition against engaging in commerce with produce of the Sabbatical Year is not one of the primary prohibitions of the Sabbatical Year, and yet its punishment is harsh.

notes.he: הסוחר בפירות שביעית. ולהכי קרי ליה אבק שאין זו עיקר מצותה של איסור שביעית:
notes.en: The dust of the Sabbatical Year: one who trades in Sabbatical-Year produce. It is called “dust” because this is not the core of the Sabbatical-Year prohibition.

notes.he: פירוש דהיינו סחורה דאין זה עיקר האיסור דעיקר האיסור הוא חרישה וזריעה ואם תאמר ומנלן דעל ידי סחורה בלבד קלקולים אלו שמפרש כאן באין עליו דלמא על ידי חרישה וזריעה דוקא הם באים וי"ל דהיינו מדה כנגד מדה ע"י שמכר פירות שביעית הוא מוכר את אשר לו:
notes.en: How severe is the dust of the Sabbatical Year: meaning, this is trading, which is not the main prohibition; the main prohibition is plowing and sowing. And if you ask: From where do we know that these misfortunes explained here come upon him through trading alone? Perhaps they come only through plowing and sowing? One can say that this is measure for measure: because he sold Sabbatical-Year produce, he sells what is his.

messages.text: If a person has commercial dealings with produce of the Sabbatical Year or of the Jubilee Year, ultimately he will become so poor that he will be compelled to sell his movable property, as it is stated: “In this Jubilee Year you shall return every man to his possession” (Leviticus 25:13),

verse.he: בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל הַזֹּאת תָּשֻׁבוּ אִישׁ אֶל־אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: In this year of jubilee, each of you shall return to your holding.

notes.he: אבקה כמו ריח איסור שביעית כלומר שעיקר איסור שביעית הוא זהו שמאצר פירות שביעית עד שמיטה וסוחרין בפירות שביעית אינו עיקר איסור שביעית אלא דקא דרשינן לקרא לאכלה ולא לסחורה ואעפ"כ גורם אותו עון שמוכר מטלטליו דכתיב וכי תמכרו ממכר וי"ו מוסיף על ענין ראשון שמכירה זו באה על עון מכירת פירות שביעית. (לא באת) [לא הרגיש]. שלא נתחרט בו אלא חזר ומכר עוד:
notes.en: The dust of the Sabbatical Year: “dust” as in a whiff of the Sabbatical-Year prohibition. That is, the main prohibition of the Sabbatical Year is one who hoards Sabbatical-Year produce until the shemitta, whereas trading in Sabbatical-Year produce is not the main prohibition of the Sabbatical Year; we only expound the verse, “for eating” and not for trading. Even so, that sin causes him to sell his movables, as it is written, “And if you sell something”: the vav [“and”] adds to the previous matter, [teaching] that this sale comes because of the sin of selling Sabbatical-Year produce. He did not feel: that he did not regret it, but went back and sold more.

messages.text: and it is written in the subsequent verse: “And if you sell something to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor’s hand,” which is referring to an item acquired by passing it from hand to hand. The juxtaposition of the two verses indicates that if one violates the halakhot of the Jubilee Year or the Sabbatical Year, he will eventually have to sell his movable property.

verse.he: וְכִי־תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ אוֹ קָנֹה מִיַּד עֲמִיתֶךָ אַל־תּוֹנוּ אִישׁ אֶת־אָחִיו׃
verse.en: When you sell property to your neighbor, or buy any from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.

notes.he: ודרשי' סמוכין והכי אמר רחמנא אם לא תשמרו מצות יובל סופכם למכור מטלטלין וכלי תשמיש:
notes.en: And next to it, “And if you sell something”: and we expound juxtapositions. This is what the Merciful One said: If you do not keep the mitzvot of the Jubilee, in the end you will sell movables and household utensils.

messages.text: If he does not feel remorse and he does not repent, ultimately he will be compelled to sell his fields, as it is stated in an adjacent verse: “If your brother becomes poor and sells part of his ancestral land” (Leviticus 25:25).

verse.he: כִּי־יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ וּמָכַר מֵאֲחֻזָּתוֹ וּבָא גֹאֲלוֹ הַקָּרֹב אֵלָיו וְגָאַל אֵת מִמְכַּר אָחִיו׃
verse.en: If one of your kin is in straits and has to sell part of a holding, the nearest redeemer shall come and redeem what that relative has sold.

notes.he: לא נזדעזע לשוב מן העבירה:
notes.en: He did not feel: he was not shaken to turn back from the transgression.

messages.text: If consciousness of his sins does not come to him, ultimately he will be compelled to sell his house, as it is stated: “And if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city” (Leviticus 25:29).

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִמְכֹּר בֵּית־מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ עַד־תֹּם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ יָמִים תִּהְיֶה גְאֻלָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone who sells a dwelling house in a walled city: It may be redeemed until a year has elapsed since its sale; the redemption period shall be a year.

notes.he: משמע שלא יעלה על לבו שיהא עושה שום עבירה:
notes.en: It did not come to his hand: this implies that it does not even enter his mind that he is committing any transgression.

messages.text: What is different there, in the previous clause, where the tanna says that the sinner does not sense remorse, and what is different here, where he says that consciousness of his sins does not come to him? This is in accordance with the statement of Rav Huna, as Rav Huna says:
Once a person commits a transgression and repeats it, it is permitted to him.

Can it enter your mind to say that it is actually permitted to him because he has transgressed twice? Rather, say that it becomes as though it were permitted to him, that is, after transgressing the prohibition twice he becomes accustomed to this behavior and no longer feels that it is a sin.
If one transgresses the prohibition only once, he is apt to feel remorse. Once he repeats his transgression, he loses this sensibility concerning his sins and will no longer feel any remorse.

notes.he: דומה בעיניו כהיתר. הלכך ברישא דלא עבר עדיין אלא פעם אחת תני הרגיש דמשמע שהיה יודע ונותן אל לבו שהיה עובר אבל לא נרתע מן העבירה ועשאה ובפעם שניה תני לא באת לידו שאפילו על לבו אין עולה שתהא עבירה:
notes.en: It becomes to him as permitted: it seems in his eyes like something permitted. Therefore, in the first clause, where he has so far transgressed only once, it teaches “he did not feel,” which implies that he knew and took to heart that he was transgressing, but did not recoil from the transgression and did it. And the second time it teaches “it did not come to his hand,” that it does not even rise in his mind that it is a transgression.

messages.text: If consciousness of his sins does not come to him, ultimately he will be compelled to borrow with interest, as it is stated: “And if your brother becomes poor and his means fail with you, then you shall uphold him” (Leviticus 25:35), and it is written in the subsequent verse: “You shall take no interest or increase from him.”

verse.he: וְכִי־יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ וּמָטָה יָדוֹ עִמָּךְ וְהֶחֱזַקְתָּ בּוֹ גֵּר וְתוֹשָׁב וָחַי עִמָּךְ׃
verse.en: If your kin, being in straits, come under your authority, and are held by you as though resident aliens, let them live by your side:

messages.text: One does not come to borrow with interest until he has already been compelled to sell his daughter, as it is stated: “And when a man sells his daughter as a maidservant” (Exodus 21:7).

verse.he: וְכִי־יִמְכֹּר אִישׁ אֶת־בִּתּוֹ לְאָמָה לֹא תֵצֵא כְּצֵאת הָעֲבָדִים׃
verse.en: When someone sells their daughter as a slave, she shall not go free as other slaves do.

notes.he: כלומר שמאחר ששנה בעבירה דומה לו כהיתר ואינו משים על לבו לחזור עוד בתשובה [זהו לא באתה לידו. ואע"ג דבתו בהאי ענינא לא כתיב ניחא ליה לאינש כלומר מוטב היה לו שימכור בתו קודם שילוה ברבית דאילו בתו אם השיגה ידו שתפדה עצמה או שפודה אחר מקרוביה מגרעת פדיונה ויוצאה כמו עבד עברי שמנכה שני עבדותה ומנכה מדמיה. והלוה ברבית מוסיף ונותן על הקרן הרבית]:
notes.en: It did not come to his hand: that is, since he repeated the transgression, it seems to him as permitted, and he does not set his heart to return in repentance; [that is “it did not come to his hand.” And even though his daughter is not written in this passage, a person prefers: that is, it is better for him to sell his daughter before he borrows with interest. For his daughter, if her hand attains so that she redeems herself, or another of her relatives redeems her, deducts from her redemption payment and goes free, like a Hebrew slave, where one deducts the years of her servitude from her price; whereas one who borrows with interest adds the interest on top of the principal and pays it.]

messages.text: And even though his daughter is not mentioned in that context in Leviticus, nevertheless, a person prefers to sell his daughter and not to borrow money with interest. This is because there, when one sells his daughter, the sum required in order to redeem her continuously decreases, while here, where one borrows with interest, his debt continuously increases. One may therefore assume that if one borrows with interest, he has already sold his daughter.

notes.dh: ניחא ליה לאיניש דליזבין ברתיה ולא לוזיף בריביתא
notes.he: דריבית כתיב בהאי ענינא דכתיב (ויקרא כה) אל תקח מאתו נשך ותרבית וגו' והא ודאי מקמי הכי כבר זבנה לברתיה דבהכי ניחא ליה:
notes.en: A person prefers to sell his daughter and not to borrow with interest: interest is written in this passage, as it is written (Leviticus 25:36), “Take no interest or increase from him…”; and certainly before this he had already sold his daughter, since he prefers that.

notes.he: שסתם מכירת הבת אינה שתהא שפחה אלא עד שיגיעו ימי נערות ואם בא לפדותה בתוך כך מחשב הדמים שמכרה כמה מגיע לכל שנה שהיתה ראויה להיות ביד האדון ולפי אותו חשבון המגיע לכל שנה מנכה לו האדון לכל שנה ושנה ששמשתו כדתניא בקדושין (דף יא.) והפדה מלמד שמגרעת פדיונה ויוצאה:
notes.en: The redemption of his daughter keeps decreasing: for an ordinary sale of a daughter is only for her to be a maidservant until her days of young womanhood arrive. If he comes to redeem her in the meantime, he calculates how much of the money for which he sold her falls to each year she was to be in the master’s hand, and according to that yearly amount the master deducts for him for each year that she served him, as it is taught in Kiddushin (11a): “Then he shall let her be redeemed” (Exodus 21:8) teaches that she deducts from her redemption payment and goes free.

messages.text: If consciousness of his sins does not come to him, ultimately he will be compelled to sell himself, as it is stated: “And when your brother becomes poor with you and sells himself to you” (Leviticus 25:39).

verse.he: וְכִי־יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ וְנִמְכַּר־לָךְ לֹא־תַעֲבֹד בּוֹ עֲבֹדַת עָבֶד׃
verse.en: If your kin under you continue in straits and must be given over to you, do not subject them to the treatment of a slave.

messages.text: Not only will he be sold to you, a born Jew; rather, he will even be sold to a stranger, as it is stated: “And sells himself to the stranger” (Leviticus 25:47). And not only to a stranger who is a convert, but even to a gentile who resides in Eretz Yisrael and observes the seven Noahide mitzvot [ger toshav], as it is stated: “And sells himself to a ger toshav with you” (Leviticus 25:47).

verse.he: וְכִי תַשִּׂיג יַד גֵּר וְתוֹשָׁב עִמָּךְ וּמָךְ אָחִיךָ עִמּוֹ וְנִמְכַּר לְגֵר תּוֹשָׁב עִמָּךְ אוֹ לְעֵקֶר מִשְׁפַּחַת גֵּר׃
verse.en: If a resident alien among you has prospered, and your kin, being in straits, comes under that one’s authority and is given over to the resident alien among you, or to an offshoot of an alien’s family,

notes.he: לא לך אלא לגר כלומר [פעמים] שלא יזכה שימכור לך אלא לגר שזה זילות מרובה שעובד לגר:
notes.en: Not to you, but to a stranger: that is, [at times] he does not merit to be sold to you, but to a stranger, which is a great degradation, that he serves a stranger.

notes.he: שאינו גר לכל דבר אלא שכופר בעבודת כוכבים:
notes.en: To a ger toshav: who is not a convert in every respect, but only renounces idol worship.

messages.text: When the verse further states: “Or to the offshoot of a stranger’s family,” this is referring to the gentile relatives of a ger toshav, who are idolaters. When it says: “Or to the offshoot [le’eker] of a stranger’s family,” this is referring to one who is sold and becomes a servant to idol worship itself, i.e., he is put to work in a temple dedicated to idolatry.

notes.he: שהיה נעשה משרת לעבודת כוכבים לחטוב עצים ולשאוב מים:
notes.en: And becomes a servant: who would become a servant to idol worship, to chop wood and draw water.

notes.dh: או לעקר זה הנמכר לעבודת כוכבים עצמה
notes.he: לפי שסופן של עבודות כוכבים ליעקר דריש הכי:
notes.en: Or to the offshoot [le’eker]: this is one who is sold to idol worship itself. It expounds it so because the end of idolatries is to be uprooted [le’akker].

notes.he: שיהא מכבד ומרבץ לפניה והיינו לעקר שנעקר לצורך עבודת כוכבים. והואיל ומפני עון שסוחר בפירות שביעית גורם שנמכר נחמיר עליו עוד וכשיגאל תהא ידו על התחתונה:
notes.en: This is one sold to idol worship itself: that he sweeps and sprinkles [the floor] before it; and that is le’eker, that he is uprooted for the needs of idol worship. And since he caused himself to be sold through the sin of trading in Sabbatical-Year produce, we will be still more stringent with him, and when he is redeemed his hand will be the lower.

messages.caption: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina: step by step, the verses of Leviticus 25 that follow one who trades in Sabbatical-Year produce.

messages.text: In any event, the baraita teaches that it is only due to an individual’s sins that he reaches such a low point that he must sell himself as a slave. If so, the verses dealing with a Hebrew slave should be interpreted in a stringent manner, so that the slave cannot easily be redeemed.
But the verse subsequently restores him, i.e., it requires that one strive to redeem him from slavery. As the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
messages.quote: the verses dealing with a Hebrew slave should be interpreted in a stringent manner

notes.he: אביי לההוא מרבנן אפ"ה הא אהדריה קרא שיהו מרחמין עליו:
notes.en: He said to him: Abaye [said] to that Sage: Even so, the verse brought him back, so that they should have mercy on him.

notes.he: אמר ליה הא אהדריה קרא שחס הכתוב עליו לאחר מכאן דקאמר קרא גאולה תהיה וביובל יצא אחר שנמכר והואיל ואהדריה קרא וחס (נמי) עליה ונגאל ידו על העליונה:
notes.en: He said to him: But the verse brought him back, for the verse had mercy on him afterward, as the verse says, “he shall have redemption,” and “in the Jubilee he shall go out,” after he was sold. And since the verse brought him back and had mercy on him [the text here is garbled; a marginal note reads “and had mercy on him”], therefore when he is redeemed, too, it has mercy on him and his hand is the upper.

messages.text: Since he went and sold himself to a temple dedicated to idol worship, should I throw a stone after the fallen? In other words, perhaps he should be left to his own devices? The verse states: He shall have a perpetual right of redemption, and he shall leave in the Jubilee (see Leviticus 25:31, 48).

notes.he: כלומר שלא יגאל לעולם:
notes.en: Should I throw a stone: that is, that he should never be redeemed.

messages.text: Even so, you can say that he shall have a redemption so that he will not be assimilated among the gentiles, but actually, with regard to his redemption we will be stringent, as it is due only to his sins that he is enslaved.

notes.he: עליה שאם נמכר במנה והשביח יחשב במאתים או אם נמכר במאתים והכסיף יחשב במאתים כדכתיב (שם) מכסף מקנתו:
notes.en: We will be stringent: with him, so that if he was sold for a maneh and appreciated, he is calculated at two hundred; or if he was sold for two hundred and depreciated, he is calculated at two hundred, as it is written (ibid.), “from the money of his purchase.”

messages.text: Two verses are written with regard to redeeming someone who was sold to a gentile. It is written: “If there are yet many in the years, according to them he shall return the price of his redemption from the money that he was bought for” (Leviticus 25:51). And it is written in the next verse: “And if there remain but few in the years until the Jubilee Year, then he shall reckon with him; according to his years he shall return the price of his redemption.”

verse.he: אִם־עוֹד רַבּוֹת בַּשָּׁנִים לְפִיהֶן יָשִׁיב גְּאֻלָּתוֹ מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ׃
verse.en: If many years remain, [your kin] shall pay back for the redemption in proportion to the purchase price;

messages.text: Now, are there years with much time and years with little time? Every year is the same length.

notes.he: שתהא שנה יתירה מחבירתה דקאמר קרא אם עוד רבות בשנים או שנה פחותה מחבירתה:
notes.en: Are there many years: that one year should be longer than another, so that the verse says “if there are yet many in the years,” or a year shorter than another?

notes.dh: וכי יש שנים מרובות או שנים מעוטות
notes.he: בשמיטה אחת יותר מבאחרת אלא כך פירושו אם נתרבה כספו בשני עבודתו כגון ששבח כשהוא נגאל מחשב אחר כסף מקנתו כדכתיב ואם עוד רבות בשנים לפיהן ישיב את גאולתו מכסף מקנתו:
notes.en: And are there many years or few years in one Sabbatical cycle more than in another? Rather, this is its meaning: if his money increased in the years of his service, e.g., he appreciated, when he is redeemed one calculates by the money of his purchase, as it is written, “If there are yet many in the years, according to them he shall return the price of his redemption from the money of his purchase.”

messages.text: Rather, this means that if his monetary value appreciated during the years of his service, he is redeemed according to “the money that he was bought for,” which is the lower sum. And if his monetary value depreciated over time, one determines his value “according to his years,” i.e., according to his current value rather than according to his previous worth. The verse indicates that one acts leniently when calculating the redemption payment of a Hebrew slave.

notes.he: הכי קאמר קרא אם יש ריבוי בכספו בשנים שהוא עומד בהן כלומר מה שהשביחו ישיב גאולתו מכסף מקנתו דאין מחשב אלא כמה שנמכר ואם מעט נשארו דמיו בשנים שהוא עומד בהן כגון שהכסיף כפי שניו ישיב את גאולתו:
notes.en: Rather: this is what the verse says: If there is an increase in his money in the years in which he stands, that is, he appreciated, he returns his redemption “from the money of his purchase,” for one calculates only by what he was sold for. And if his money remained little in the years in which he stands, e.g., he depreciated, he returns his redemption “according to his years.”

notes.he: כגון שהכסיף יהיב בתר (השתא) [השנים] כפי שניו כמו ששוה עכשיו היינו ואם מעט נשאר בשנים וגו' ומהכא ילפינן בפירוש דנגאל וידו על העליונה:
notes.en: And if his money decreased: e.g., he depreciated, he gives according to [the years], “according to his years,” as he is worth now; that is, “And if there remain but few in the years…” And from here we learn explicitly that he is redeemed and his hand is the upper.

messages.text: But say that the verses should be interpreted as follows: “If there are yet many in the years,” is referring to a case where he served for two years, and four years of servitude remain. In this situation let him return to his master the value of four years of his servitude according to “the money that he was bought for.”

notes.he: הכי קאמר קרא היכא דפלח ליה תרתי שני ופשו ארבעי עד יובל ליתיב ליה כמה שמגיע לארבע שנים מכסף מקנתו לפי חשבון שקנאו:
notes.en: But say: this is what the verse says: Where he served him two years and four remain until the Jubilee, let him give him as much as falls to four years “from the money of his purchase,” according to the calculation by which he bought him.

notes.dh: ואימא היכא דעבד תרתי ופיישי ד' כו'
notes.he: פירש רש"י ולא בהכסיף והשביח מישתעי מידי ול"נ דא"כ אין זה כי אם מפשטיה דקרא ובלא ייתור שמעינן ליה ומשמע דרב נחמן בר יצחק מיתורא קא מפיק לכן נראה לפרש ואימא היכא דעבד תרתי ופייש ארבע ניתיב ליה ארבע מכסף מקנתו בין הכסיף בין השביח והיכא דעבד ארבע ופייש ליה תרתי ניתיב ליה תרתי כפי שניו בין הכסיף בין השביח ולהכי אתא יתורא דקרא דלעולם אחר הסמוך אזלינן:
notes.en: But say: where he served two and four remain, etc.: Rashi explained that the verse does not speak of depreciation and appreciation at all. But this does not seem right to me, for if so, this would be nothing but the plain sense of the verse, and we would learn it without the superfluous word, whereas it implies that Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak derives it from the superfluous word. Therefore it seems right to explain: But say: where he served two and four remain, let him give him four “from the money of his purchase,” whether he depreciated or appreciated; and where he served four and two remain, let him give him two “according to his years,” whether he depreciated or appreciated. And for this the superfluous word of the verse comes: that we always go by the nearer one.

messages.text: And the phrase “if there remain but few in the years” is referring to a case where he served for four years and two years of servitude remain. In this situation let him return to his master the value of two years of his servitude “according to his years.”

notes.he: לפי שנים שהיה עדיין חייב לעובדו ולאו בהכסיף והשביח משתעי קרא:
notes.en: According to his years: according to the years he still owed to serve him; and the verse does not speak of depreciation and appreciation at all.

notes.he: ואימא [להכי אתו הני קראי] דהיכא דעבד תרתי [שני דשמיטה ופיישי תו ארבע שני ופודהו (נגאל) יהיב ליה דמי דארבעי שני לבעליו] מכסף מקנתו שנתן בשבילו והיינו אם עוד רבות בשנים שעבד פחות מחצי שבוע שיתן לו דמי ד' שנים (שנשארו) לפי חשבון שקנאו ואם מעט נשאר בשנים היינו היכא דעבד ארבע [ופיישי תרתי ועכשיו הוא נגאל ליתן ליה דמי דתרתי שני והיינו כפי שניו כלומר כפי מעוט שנים שנשתיירו ולהכי הוא דאתו ולא להקל עליו כדקא דרשת:
notes.en: But say [these verses come for this]: where he served two [years of the seven and four more years remain, and he redeems himself, he gives his owner the value of four years] “from the money of his purchase,” which was given for him. That is, “if there are yet many in the years”: he served less than half of the seven, so he gives him the value of four years according to the calculation by which he bought him. And “if there remain but few in the years” is where he served four and two remain, and now he is redeemed, he gives him the value of two years; and that is “according to his years,” that is, according to the few years that remain. For this they come, and not to be lenient with him as you expounded.

messages.text: If so, let the verse write: If there are yet many years. What is the meaning of the phrase “in the years”?
messages.quote: where he served for two years, and four years of servitude remain

notes.he: הוא דלהכי אתו לכתוב אם עוד רבות שנים:
notes.en: If so: that they come for this, let it write, “if there are yet many years.”

messages.text: Rather, this indicates that if his monetary value appreciated in the years of his service, he is redeemed according to “the money that he was bought for,” which is the lower sum. If his monetary value depreciated in the years, one determines his value “according to his years,” i.e., according to his current value.

notes.he: ש"מ דאם נתרבה כספו בשנים שהשביח יהיב מכסף מקנתו להקל כדאמרן]:
notes.en: What is “in the years”? Conclude from it that if his money increased in the years, that he appreciated, he gives “from the money of his purchase,” to be lenient, as we said.

messages.text: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak interpreted these verses as truly as if the interpretation had been transmitted to Moses from Sinai.

notes.he: כסיני דהכי פירושיהן:
notes.en: Like Sinai: that this is their meaning.

messages.text: One may not sell his ancestral field that is located in a distant area and redeem with that money a field that he sold in a nearby area. Likewise, he may not sell a low-quality field and redeem with that money a high-quality field. And he may not borrow money and redeem the field, nor may he redeem the field incrementally, half now and half at a later date.

notes.he: כדפרשינן לעיל:
notes.en: He may not sell far away, etc.: as we explained above.

messages.text: From where are these matters derived? As the Sages taught with regard to the verse: “And he prospers and finds sufficient means to redeem it” (Leviticus 25:26):
messages.quote: One may not sell his ancestral field that is located in a distant area

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי לֹא יִהְיֶה־לּוֹ גֹּאֵל וְהִשִּׂיגָה יָדוֹ וּמָצָא כְּדֵי גְאֻלָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone who has no one to be redeemer but prospers and acquires enough to redeem with:

messages.text: The phrase “and he prospers” teaches that the money he uses to redeem the field must be his own possession, meaning that he may not borrow money and redeem the field.

notes.he: כלומר אם השיג משלו ולא שילוה:
notes.en: “And his hand attains”: his own hand; that is, if he attained from his own [means], and not that he borrows.

messages.text: “And finds sufficient means”; this excludes the usage of means that were previously available, meaning that one may not sell property that he owned at the time of the sale in order to redeem his field, e.g., he may not sell a field that is located in a distant area and redeem a field that is located in a nearby area, nor may he sell a low-quality field and redeem a high-quality field.

notes.he: מאחר שמכר פרט למצוי שלא ימכור מה שהיה לו קודם לכן כגון שלא ימכור ברחוק כו':
notes.en: And finds: after he sold; excluding what was available, that he may not sell what he had before that, e.g., he may not sell far away, etc.

messages.text: “Sufficient means to redeem it”; this indicates that one may redeem his field if he possesses sufficient means to redeem the entire field, but he may not partially redeem his field.

notes.he: כלומר אם השיג כדי לגאול הכל בבת אחת גואל ואינו רשאי לגאול לחצאין:
notes.en: Sufficient means to redeem it: that is, if he attained enough to redeem all of it at once, he redeems, and he is not permitted to redeem by halves.

messages.text: Is this to say that the term “finds” indicates that the means were found now and were not previously available? But you can raise a contradiction to this premise from a baraita:
messages.quote: “And finds sufficient means”; this excludes the usage of means that were previously available

notes.he: דומצא דכתיב והשיגה ידו ומצא דהשתא משמע כלומר שמצא מאחר שמכר:
notes.en: Is this to say: that “and finds,” written in “and his hand attains and finds,” implies now, that is, that he found after he sold?

messages.text: The verse states with regard to an unintentional killer: “And one who goes into the forest with another to hew wood, and his hand fetches a stroke with the ax to cut down the tree, and the blade slips off the wood, and finds another person, and he dies, he shall flee to one of these cities and live” (Deuteronomy 19:5). The term “and finds” excludes one who introduces himself into the area of danger.

verse.he: וַאֲשֶׁר יָבֹא אֶת־רֵעֵהוּ בַיַּעַר לַחְטֹב עֵצִים וְנִדְּחָה יָדוֹ בַגַּרְזֶן לִכְרֹת הָעֵץ וְנָשַׁל הַבַּרְזֶל מִן־הָעֵץ וּמָצָא אֶת־רֵעֵהוּ וָמֵת הוּא יָנוּס אֶל־אַחַת הֶעָרִים־הָאֵלֶּה וָחָי׃
verse.en: For instance, a man goes with another fellow into a grove to cut wood; as his hand swings the ax to cut down a tree, the ax-head flies off the handle and strikes the other so that he dies. That man shall flee to one of these cities and live.—

notes.he: שהיה חבירו מצוי שם בשעה שהרים זה הגרזן חייב פרט לממציא את עצמו דפטור זה מגלות:
notes.en: And finds another, and he dies: where his fellow was present there at the time this one raised the ax, he is liable [to exile]; excluding one who introduces himself, for whom this one is exempt from exile.

notes.he: את רעהו ומת והוא ינוס שנמצא כבר הוא פרט לאם המציא את עצמו שפטור:
notes.en: “And finds another and he dies,” and he is a victim of circumstance, for [the other] was already present; excluding one who introduced himself, for then he is exempt.

messages.text: If, after the stone departed from one’s hand, the other person stuck his head out and received a blow from it and died, the killer is exempt from exile.
Evidently, the term “finds” indicates an item that is there from the outset.
Here, “finds” is interpreted according to the context of the verse, and here it is likewise interpreted according to the context of the verse.

Here, with regard to redeeming a field, one interprets “finds” in a manner similar to the phrase “he prospers.” Just as “he prospers” is referring to funds that he acquires only now, so too “finds” indicates property that he finds only now, and not property that he owned from the outset.

notes.he: דודאי מעיקרא כשמכרה לא היתה ידו משגת כדכתיב (שם) כי ימוך אחיך ומכר מאחוזתו:
