notes.en: Just as “his hand attains” is now: for certainly at first, when he sold it, his hand did not attain, as it is written (ibid.): “If your brother becomes poor and sells part of his ancestral land.”

notes.he: משמע לאחר שמכר דאם השיגה בשעת מכירה לא הוה מוכר:
notes.en: Just as “and his hand attains” implies after he sold, for had it attained at the time of sale, he would not have sold.

messages.text: And here, with regard to an unintentional killer, one interprets “finds” in a manner similar to the term “forest.” Just as a forest is something that is there from the outset, so too, “finds” indicates something, i.e., an individual, that is there from the outset. This excludes an individual who was not in the vicinity when the ax slipped.

But with regard to redeeming a field from the Temple treasury, it is permitted to redeem the field in any of these ways. This is a halakha where greater stringency applies with regard to redeeming a field from an ordinary individual than with regard to redeeming it from the Temple treasury.
From where are these matters derived? As the Sages taught with regard to a verse dealing with one who consecrates his field:
messages.quote: it is permitted to redeem the field in any of these ways

messages.text: “And if the one who consecrates the field will indeed redeem it” (Leviticus 27:19). The phrase “will indeed redeem” teaches that one may borrow money and redeem his field, and one may partially redeem his field, despite the fact that one may not do so when redeeming a field from an ordinary individual.

verse.he: וְאִם־גָּאֹל יִגְאַל אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֹתוֹ וְיָסַף חֲמִשִׁית כֶּסֶף־עֶרְכְּךָ עָלָיו וְקָם לוֹ׃
verse.en: and if the one who consecrated the land wishes to redeem it, one-fifth must be added to the sum at which it was assessed, and it shall be passed back.

notes.dh: ואם גאל יגאל המקדיש וגו' מלמד שלוה
notes.he: מאחר וגואל ואם ירצה יגאל לחצאין:
notes.en: “And if the one who consecrates will indeed redeem…” teaches that he borrows: from another and redeems, and if he wishes, he redeems by halves.

notes.he: משמע נמי השתא אחר שמכר ובהקדש מותר בכולן למכור כר' ול"ג בקדש וכן כולן זה חומר בהדיוט מבהקדש (בהקדש) שרשאי לעשות כל אלו להוציאו מיד הקדש]:
notes.en: So too “and finds” also implies now, after he sold. And with consecrated property he is permitted in all of them, to sell, etc. (And we do not read “in the sacred.”) And so all of them: “This is a stringency with an ordinary person over consecrated property,” that he is permitted to do all of these to take it out of the hand of the Temple treasury.

messages.text: What is the reason for this leniency in the case of consecrated fields? It is because we find with regard to one who sells his ancestral field, that the Torah enhanced his power, in that if the Jubilee Year arrived and the field was not redeemed, it returns to its original owners in the Jubilee Year.
Therefore, his power was diminished with regard to the manner of redemption, in that he cannot borrow money and redeem the field, and he cannot partially redeem it.

notes.he: כדאמרן לעיל:
notes.en: His power was diminished: as we said above.

notes.he: שאינו לוה וגואל כדאמרן:
notes.en: His power was diminished: in that he does not borrow and redeem, as we said.

messages.text: But with regard to one who consecrates his ancestral field, since his power was diminished, in that if the Jubilee Year arrived and the field was not redeemed, the field leaves the possession of the Temple treasury and passes to the possession of the priests and does not return to the original owner, the Torah therefore enhanced his power, in that he may borrow money and redeem his field, and he may partially redeem it.

notes.he: (אף כך) [אבל] במקדיש שדה אחוזה הואיל והורע כחו בענין אחר יפה כחו בענין אחד הלכך בהקדש מותר בכולן:
notes.en: [But] with one who consecrates an ancestral field: since his power was diminished in another respect, his power was enhanced in this one respect; therefore with consecrated property he is permitted in all of them.

messages.text: Continues on 31a: the Gemara contrasts two baraitot, one teaching that one may borrow and partially redeem a consecrated field and one that one may not, and explains that one follows the Rabbis and the other Rabbi Shimon. Then a new mishna: one who sells a house in a walled city.
